name: Uniqode
summary: Dynamic QR codes and digital business cards with real-time scan analytics — connect offline touchpoints to measurable results and capture leads.
best_for: marketing teams that need dynamic QR codes with real analytics and enterprise compliance (SOC 2, GDPR, ISO 27001, optional HIPAA)
skip_if: you only need the occasional static QR code — a free generator does that, and Bitly is better if link-shortening is your main job
honest_knock: The tier jumps are steep and a lot is gated: analytics are capped at 60 days on the entry plan, scan limits apply across all tiers, and custom domains sit behind higher pricing. It's a real QR platform — but overkill if you just want the occasional code.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-09-13 on their own pricing page, read both as plain HTML and as a live browser render) The plan cards are rendered in the browser and carry no price in either reading, so what we can hold Uniqode to is its own pricing FAQ on that page, read 13 September 2026. Static QR codes are free and there is no limit on how many you create; dynamic QR codes start at a stated minimum of $9/month. NEW since our August reading: the FAQ now prices one named tier, Core at $49/month, which it calls the best value -- it does not say where Core sits in the Starter, Lite, Pro, Plus and Business+ ladder the same FAQ uses elsewhere. A custom domain is a Plus add-on at $2,000 per domain per year. Your first digital business card is free, with extra seats on a Team plan at $6 per user per month; Business+ card pricing is custom. There is a 14-day free trial, and when it expires the dynamic codes made during it go inactive while static codes keep working (without account access). Billing is annual only, in USD, invoice billing is Business+ only, and there is a 30-day money-back guarantee. Third-party listings quote a $5 entry tier; that is not what Uniqode's own page says, and we are not repeating a Lite or Pro figure we could not read at the source.
